title: Aftermath and Language
premise: Quentin Dravenmoor, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost the ability to taste after a family betrayal he refuses to name, is assigned to profile Odile Vasseur, the last fluent speaker of Lumençal, a dying language of her isolated coastal valley. As she teaches him words for things he can no longer feel—salt, sweetness, forgiveness—their lessons become an intimacy that forces Quentin to confront his estranged sister Marthe, whose ambition destroyed both their family restaurant and his senses. When Odile's health fails and developers move to raze the valley, Quentin must choose between publishing the exposé that would save the village and expose Marthe, or protecting the sister he still loves. In the end, he speaks Lumençal at a public hearing, sacrificing his anonymity and career; Marthe confesses, the valley wins a reprieve, and Quentin tastes salt on his own lips for the first time in years as Odile dies content, her language carried in one imperfect student.
about_author: Mirabel Amberdale is the pen name of a former line cook turned archivist who spent three years documenting endangered dialects along the Atlantic coast. Aftermath and Language is their second novel, following the acclaimed The Salt Ledger.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A wry, controlled opening: Quentin reviews a lavish tasting menu he cannot taste, writing brilliant prose from texture and memory alone. His editor assigns him a human-interest profile of a dying language's last speaker. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: A Grammar of Salt
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. He travels to the valley of Cendrillon-sur-Mer and meets Odile Vasseur, sharp-tongued and unimpressed by his fame. She agrees to teach him only if he learns to describe food honestly—which he cannot do. First lesson: the word for salt. Beat: reluctant connection.

chapters.title: Words That Refuse Translation
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Through her eyes we see Quentin's evasions and the village's suspicion of outsiders. She recognizes a fellow keeper of silences. Lessons deepen; he almost describes a flavor truthfully, then retreats. Beat: tenderness meeting resistance.

chapters.title: What Marthe Built
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Flashback braided with present: the family restaurant, the fire, the contract Marthe signed with the Halvard development group, the accusation Quentin never voiced. He realizes Halvard is behind the valley's demolition permits. Beat: dread surfacing.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Her health falters; the doctor's visit is hidden from Quentin. She begins recording a dictionary, teaching him faster, more desperately. A village child, Noé, starts eavesdropping on lessons. Beat: urgency wrapped in denial.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Enemy
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Marthe arrives in the valley to finalize the resort deal and invites Quentin to dinner, offering him redemption via a prestigious column if he stays silent about Halvard. He nearly accepts. Beat: temptation and the corruption of power wearing a loving face.

chapters.title: Everything the Mouth Can Hold
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Quentin and Odile admit what they've become to each other without saying it plainly; she teaches him the Lumençal word for 'the person you tell everything.' Marthe discovers the profile will expose her. Beat: love declared sideways, threat declared directly.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Climax. At the regional council, Quentin abandons his prepared neutral review and speaks in Lumençal, translating aloud the valley's testimony—and naming Halvard and Marthe's role. The room erupts; Marthe walks out. Beat: sacrifice of invisibility.

chapters.title: Confession in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Marthe. Shattered, she comes to Odile's cottage at night and confesses the fire and the forgery—in broken Lumençal, learned from childhood, proving the language was never only Odile's. Sisters begin the long work of reckoning. Beat: grief turning toward repair.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Language
chapters.summary: POV Quentin, coda. Months later: the valley holds a reprieve, Noé studies with recordings, Marthe serves a sentence and writes letters Quentin answers. At Odile's deathbed, Quentin tastes salt—real salt—for the first time. He speaks her eulogy in two languages. Beat: mourning, gratitude, continuation.
